sections.h2: How to pay the Pike County Sheriff
sections.html:
The sheriff's Tax Division, at 146 Main Street, Suite 204 in Pikeville, takes payment of Pike County taxes. The main number is 606-432-6260 and the tax line is 606-432-6212. Mail goes to the Pike County Sheriff's Office, Tax Division, P.O. Box 839, Pikeville, KY 41502, with checks made out to "Pike County Sheriff."

Ways to pay the Pike County Sheriff
Payment typeWhere it is accepted
CashIn person
Check or money orderAt the counter or through the post
Visa or MastercardIn person, by phone or online
Cash AppIn person, by phone or online

Online payment adds a 3% convenience fee on credit and debit cards, and the card statement shows the charge as "Kentucky Land Records." Search for the bill by number or by name, tick the box beside it, and press pay. The sheriff only collects, so questions about values and exemptions go to the Pike County Property Valuation Administrator (PVA).

Pike is Kentucky's easternmost county and its largest by land area, at 786.73 square miles. Pikeville is the seat, and Elkhorn City and Coal Run Village are the other cities. Population has been falling, and housing is inexpensive.

  • Population fell from 58,669 in 2020 to an estimated 54,721 in 2025, a 6.7% drop.
  • The 2020 census listed 28,693 housing units, 14.5% of them vacant, and 28.0% of occupied homes were rentals. The 2025 estimate is 29,481 units.
  • The median value of an owned home is $112,000, median gross rent is $858, and owner costs are $1,278 with a mortgage.
  • Household income is $44,312 at the midpoint.

With so many empty units, sellers who can show a well-kept house and a clean tax record stand out.

Pike County follows Kentucky's statewide timetable. Paying everything by November 1 earns a 2% discount, the face amount holds until year end, and a 5% penalty arrives in January. Payment after January 31 carries a 10% penalty under KRS 134.015. Taxes count as a personal debt of the owner from the day they come due.

For a mid-year sale, remember that the bill follows the deed's mailing address in the year of transfer. Call the Tax Division for the exact mailing date, because it shifts from year to year and a delayed year uses a month-by-month schedule. The sheriff's books close at the end of business on April 15, which is the cut-off for what the clerk inherits. Because the deed carries an in-care-of address for the bill in the year of transfer, give the closing agent a mailing address that will still work after the sale.

The path begins at the PVA's counter, since Kentucky bars an appeal until the owner has conferred with the PVA or a deputy. After that conference, the owner files with the county clerk no later than closing time on the workday after roll inspection ends. The roll is on view for thirteen days beginning with the first May Monday, and the local board sits between 25 and 35 days afterward.

  • Bring evidence: sales of similar homes, insurance policies, a contractor's repair estimate, photographs.
  • A paid representative must hold a qualifying professional credential, such as attorney, CPA or certified appraiser, and carry the owner's written authorization.
  • An owner may record the board hearing on audio.

The board must explain in writing any value it raises or lowers. A supplemental bill follows if the final number exceeds what the owner claimed.

Eligible owners are people 65 and up, along with anyone classed as totally disabled. For 2025 and 2026 they subtract $49,100 from the assessed value. The PVA takes the application, and a birth certificate, license or passport proves age.

If you are the seller and already hold this exemption, tell your closing agent so the proration reflects the lower bill. If you are the buyer, ask the PVA what you need to bring to apply for yourself.

sections.h2: When a Pike County tax bill goes unpaid
sections.html:
Once April 15 closes, unpaid bills pass from the sheriff to the Pike County Clerk, who records a lien and calls each bill a certificate of delinquency. Interest begins at one percent a month, and a clerk fee and county attorney fee are added. The county attorney's first notice goes out within 30 days and a second within 60, and the clerk must advertise the list in the newspaper beforehand.

For a county on the normal schedule, the sale can be set on any business day from July 14 through August 28. Clerks who also sell delinquent oil, gas or unmined mineral bills get 60 more days, with a deadline of October 27. Pike County has large coal and natural gas reserves, so a seller with mineral interests should ask the clerk whether any such bill is attached. A seller who still owes a bill should get a payoff from the clerk before listing, since a certificate bought by an investor adds substantial fees.

sections.h2: What a seller pays at closing
sections.html:
The grantor owes the transfer tax, which works out to a half dollar for every $500 block of the deed's price (KRS 142.050). The Pike County Clerk lists a deed at $50 and a mortgage at $80, with $3 added per page past the fifth for a deed.

The clerk can be reached at 606-432-6211. The Pikeville office opens Monday to Thursday from half past eight until half past four and stays open until 5:30 on Fridays. Three branch offices keep shorter schedules:

  • Belfry: Tuesday 9:00 to 4:00 and Friday 9:00 to 6:00.
  • Phelps: Monday 9:00 to 4:00 and Wednesday 9:00 to 5:30.
  • Elkhorn City: Tuesday 9:00 to 4:00 and Thursday 9:00 to 5:30.

The clerk's deed page lists what a deed must carry, including a notarized consideration statement and an address for the next tax bill, so ask the closing agent to check the form first.

sections.h2: A seller's checklist for Pike County
sections.html:
1. Call the Tax Division at 606-432-6212 and confirm this year's bill is paid and nothing older is open.
  2. Ask the clerk, 606-432-6211, whether a certificate of delinquency is recorded against the parcel, and whether any oil, gas or mineral bill is attached.
  3. Choose the branch office or the Pikeville office that fits your schedule.
  4. Give the closing agent a mailing address that will still work after the sale.
  5. Ask for one total covering the deed fee, extra pages and transfer tax.

Selling for cash avoids the wait for a buyer's financing, but the lien, the recording and the tax still have to be handled at closing, so these calls apply either way.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Pike County property tax?
faqs.a: At the Pike County Sheriff's Tax Division, 146 Main Street, Suite 204, Pikeville. Payments sent by post use box 839, and the tax line is 606-432-6212.

faqs.q: Is there a fee for paying Pike County taxes by card?
faqs.a: Yes, a 3% convenience fee applies to credit and debit cards, and the charge appears as Kentucky Land Records.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a Pike County sale?
faqs.a: The seller, as grantor, at a half dollar per $500 block of the deed's price. The clerk takes it before recording.

faqs.q: When do unpaid Pike County bills reach the clerk?
faqs.a: After the close of business on April 15, when the sheriff transfers them to the county clerk as certificates of delinquency.

faqs.q: Where is the Pike County Clerk's office?
faqs.a: The clerk's number is 606-432-6211, with offices in Pikeville, Belfry, Phelps and Elkhorn City, each on its own weekly schedule.
